posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
For your first game with her, I recommend giving new players a choice between Ra, Haka, Tempest, the Wraith, or Tachyon.  Give short bios for each (e.g. "Wraith is Batman, Tachyon is the Flash, Tempest is an alien who controls thunderstorms, Haka is a Maori who smashes things, and Ra kills things with fire"), and go into more detail as players show their interest.  Choose either Baron Blade or Omnitron as the villain.  I recommend starting in Insula Primalis.  That said, I've found that it's fairly safe to let the new players choose the environment - nine times out of ten they will choose the environment described as "Dinosaurs!" on their own.  Definitely avoid Megaopolis (too many cards that say "players can't" on them).

 

Try and choose your hero(s) based on what characters/mechanics you think that your wife might find interesting (e.g. if she likes complicated puzzles play AZ.  If she likes support and tanking, play Legacy)

 

Be careful not to play the game for her - give advice about the things she wouldn't be aware of (Lightspeed Barrage, Haka of Battle, etc) and comment if she makes any drastic mistakes, but otherwise avoid providing unsolicited help (if she asks, then feel free of course).  Let her handle her own health.

I agree with everything Arcanist said. Though I would also consider Legacy a viable option for new players. He's fairly simple to play, as long as you don't mind taking a support and tanking role. I'm assuming the only heroes you have are the ones in the base game.

If one or both of you are sticklers for the rules (like I am), I'd recommend having a way to settle rules disputes. Some of the cards are ambiguously worded and in the groups I've played with arguments over the rules have gotten to be a drag. posts.name: Donner
posts.cooked:
Three hero minimum, five hero maximum.

In two player games, one or both players play two heroes.

I suggest playing Baron Blade in Insula Primalis and put two of his 3 Mobile Defense Platforms on the bottom of his deck.  Then, put one Velociraptor and one Obsidian Fields on the top of the Insual Primalis deck.  This gives a quick boost to DPS, showcases a bit of Dinsoaurs! and prevents Baron Blade from going full-defense with his MDPs (Mobile Defense Platforms).  

If you choose your heroes from Wraith, Ra, Haka, K.N.Y.F.E., Legacy, and Tempest, you have close to the demo setup we use for cons.  High damage-dealers with not too bad of buildup time (except Legacy, who is the one the demoer usually plays to support the damage dealers).  The games tend to be fast and not too complicated.

posts.cooked:
Trajector:

That's funny; most of the time the people I teach want Atlantis. 

I think that it's partially the way I introduce them.

"Megaopolis, which is Metropolis (from Superman)

Wagner Mars Base, which is… a Mars base,

Ruins of Atlantis, which is under the sea, and

Insula Primalis, which is dinosaurs."

 

When pitched like that, it encourages the players to pick "dinosaurs".  But Ruins of Atlantis would be my second choice.  In some ways it's actually better because it can add a little bit more difficulty to an easy villain (which they need if you have 5 players), and I think there's a bit more variety in effects.

Here's a list of official rules clarifications if you want to use those: http://www.spiffworld.com/sotm/files/sotm_rules_and_clarifications.pdf

Legacy's not a bad choice - I almost included him as well.  But he's often a bit more passive, which can make him a bit less fun depending on the personality and play style of the player playing him.  Exercise your judgement when deciding whether or not to include him.

If you have Young Legacy (and you can find printable versions of the cards online) then I'd definately include her (which would require included regular Legacy as well), as adding her atomic glare makes her active enough to appeal to a broader set of play styles.

posts.name: jffdougan
posts.cooked:
The big reasoning behind the conventional wisdom of "don't use Megalopolis for a first game" is that players are still learning what they CAN do. Megalopolis has cards (like Hostage Situation, Traffic Pileup, and Papparazzi on the Scene) that specifically PREVENT players from doing things that are otherwise a normal part of their turn. It interferes with the learning dynamic.

I'm going to third the suggestion of using Baron Blade as your introductory villain. He's the most straightforward villain in that he only flips once per game, introduces the flip mechanic, and introduces the nemesis mechanic if Legacy is also in the game.

For a 2-player game of rookies against Baron Blade, I'd suggest the following:

Baron Blade

Player 1: Play Legacy

Player 2: Play one hero (pick from Ra, Wraith, Haka, Tempest, Bunker. KNYFE is also good if you have her, but I'm assuming you don't)

Player 1: Play one hero (pick from same list as above)

Insula Primalis

 

If one of you focuses on running Baron Blade & one of you focuses on running Insula Primalis, that spreads the work out pretty evenly.

posts.cooked: So if me and my wife like this game what expansions should I look to get in what order?
posts.raw: So if me and my wife like this game what expansions should I look to get in what order?

posts.name: jffdougan
posts.cooked:
That will depend on what you want to get from your expansions.

The Rook City/Infernal Relics combined box probably has what are overall the hardest villains in the game in the form of the Chairman, the Ennead on advanced mode, and the Matriarch. Progeny from the Wrath of the Cosmos expansion is probably up there, but I haven't had the chance to play against it. The two heroes from Infernal Relics are also the most complicated heroes out to date. However, I love, love, love the environments from Infernal Relics.

Shattered Timelines has my favorite hero so far (Omnitron-X), along with what I consider to be an interesting environment in the form of the Block. There's a lot of love for Chrono-Ranger in the fan community, but I have yet to grok him.

Vengeance should wait, although it has another really good introductory hero in the form of KNYFE. (Sorry, Christopher, but I refuse to type out the periods.) 

I own but haven't been able to play much with Wrath of the Cosmos.
